newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel calls for Security Council meeting on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel calls for Security Council meeting on Zaire.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel called on Monday for the Security Council to hold a special meeting to discuss the humanitarian crisis in Zaire.

Kinkel said he had asked the German ambassador to the United Nations to arrange a special sitting of the Security Council and had suggested the European Union should call a meeting of development aid ministers immediately.
"Time is running out. The tragedy must be stopped," Kinkel said in a statement.
He called for an immediate ceasefire and for airports at Bukavu and Goma, now in the hands of Tutsi rebels, to be opened for aid flights.
"This is the main prerequisite for the assistance of refugees and their survival. Otherwise assistance from outside is not possible," he added.
Fighting between Tutsi rebels and the Zairean army forced the evacuation on Saturday of the last foreign aid workers and left refugees without U.N. protectors.

Sadako Ogata, the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, called on the governments of Zaire and Rwanda to help establish corridors for more than one million Hutu refugees to return in safety to their homes in Rwanda and Burundi.
Kinkel said he had appealed to the general secretary of the Organisation for African Unity to ensure the corridors were created.
